Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to their organisation's online services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive data.

Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to third-party online services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive data — review identity-provider and service access policies plus authentication test records for the named external service. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Multi-factor authentication (where available) is used to authenticate users to third-party online services that process, store or communicate their organisation's non-sensitive data — review identity-provider and service access policies plus authentication test records for the named external service. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to their organisation's online customer services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive customer data.

Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate users to third-party online customer services that process, store or communicate their organisation's sensitive customer data — review identity-provider and service access policies plus authentication test records for the named external service. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate customers to online customer services that process, store or communicate sensitive customer data.

Requests for privileged access to systems, applications and data repositories are validated when first requested — review approved privileged-access request tickets showing identity, approver, scope and first-use decision. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access.

Privileged user accounts (excluding those explicitly authorised to access online services) are prevented from accessing the internet, email and web services — review endpoint access policies and sign-in test records for privileged and unprivileged environments. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Privileged user accounts explicitly authorised to access online services are strictly limited to only what is required for users and services to undertake their duties.

Privileged users use separate privileged and unprivileged operating environments — review endpoint access policies and sign-in test records for privileged and unprivileged environments. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Unprivileged user accounts cannot logon to privileged operating environments — review endpoint access policies and sign-in test records for privileged and unprivileged environments. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Privileged user accounts (excluding local administrator accounts) cannot logon to unprivileged operating environments — review endpoint access policies and sign-in test records for privileged and unprivileged environments. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Application control restricts the execution of executables, software libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set — review workstation application-control policy, deployed rule inventory and blocked-execution test records. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Microsoft Office macro antivirus scanning is enabled — review managed Office macro policy, endpoint deployment reports and blocked-macro test records. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Restoration of data, applications and settings from backups to a common point in time is tested as part of disaster recovery exercises — review dated disaster-recovery restore exercise results identifying the common recovery point and recovered applications. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Unprivileged user accounts are prevented from modifying and deleting backups.

requirements.name: Bedrock VPC Private Connectivity
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure VPC endpoints provide private connectivity for Bedrock APIs, preventing AI traffic from traversing the public internet.

requirements.name: Network Firewall for AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure VPCs have Network Firewall enabled to inspect and filter AI workload traffic, with logging, multi-AZ deployment, and proper default actions for both full and fragmented packets.

requirements.name: WAF Protection for AI Endpoints
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure WAFv2 Web ACLs are configured with rules and logging to protect AI application endpoints from HTTP-based attacks including prompt injection patterns at the perimeter.

requirements.name: DDoS Protection for AI Infrastructure
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure AWS Shield Advanced is enabled to protect internet-facing AI application infrastructure from DDoS attacks.

requirements.name: Encryption at Rest for AI Data
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure all data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 across AI workload storage including S3 buckets, EBS volumes, RDS instances, SageMaker notebooks, and Bedrock prompts using customer-managed KMS keys where possible.

requirements.name: Encryption in Transit for AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure all data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher, including API communications, inter-container traffic for ML training, and connections between AI application components.

requirements.name: Customer-Managed Key Governance
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure customer-managed KMS keys are in use, rotation is enabled, and keys are not scheduled for unintentional deletion to maintain control over AI data encryption.

requirements.name: VPC Security for AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure VPC endpoints enforce trust boundaries, subnets do not assign public IPs by default, and flow logs are enabled for all VPCs hosting AI workloads.

requirements.name: Hardware-Enforced Compute Isolation
requirements.reason: Nitro hypervisor is a testable EC2 isolation signal. It does not cover non-EC2 AI training and inference infrastructure or operational proof that all AI workloads use isolated compute.

new_checks.data_source: ec2:DescribeInstances Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId, InstanceType, Tags; ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes InstanceTypes[].InstanceType, Hypervisor
new_checks.predicate: For each EC2 instance tagged as an in-scope AI workload, FAIL if its InstanceType joins to DescribeInstanceTypes.Hypervisor != nitro; UNKNOWN if workload tags or instance-type details are missing.
new_checks.title: Hardware-Enforced Compute Isolation
new_checks.description: Detects an EC2 instance whose EC2 InstanceType is outside the approved Nitro family; a non-Nitro hypervisor lacks the approved hardware isolation properties.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Select a Nitro-backed EC2 InstanceType for each tagged AI workload instance and redeploy it.

requirements.name: Multi-Factor Authentication for AI Access
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure MFA is enforced for all users accessing AI services, including root account hardware MFA, IAM user MFA for console access, and Cognito user pool MFA for AI application end users.

requirements.name: Least Privilege for AI Identities
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure least-privilege access is enforced for all AI service identities. No administrative privileges should be attached to IAM entities that interact with Bedrock, SageMaker, or other AI services.

requirements.name: Temporary Scoped Credentials
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure temporary and scoped credentials are used for AI service access. Long-term access keys should be avoided, rotated within 90 days when necessary, and unused keys should be disabled.

requirements.name: Root Account Security
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure root account is properly secured with no active access keys and minimal usage, as root credentials in AI environments could grant unrestricted access to all AI models, data, and agent configurations.

requirements.name: AI Service Role Security
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure IAM roles used for AI services prevent cross-service confused deputy attacks and stale access to Bedrock and SageMaker is reviewed regularly.

requirements.name: Password Policy for AI Service Access
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure strong password policies are enforced with minimum length, complexity requirements, expiration, and reuse prevention for all human identities accessing AI services.

requirements.name: Cognito User Authentication for AI Apps
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Cognito user pools are properly configured for AI application user authentication with advanced security features, token revocation, self-registration controls, and WAF protection.

requirements.name: API Authorization for AI Endpoints
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure API Gateway endpoints serving AI applications have proper authorization configured to authenticate and authorize every request to the model layer.

requirements.name: Data Classification for AI
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Amazon Macie is enabled with automated sensitive data discovery to classify and protect enterprise data before it is made available to AI systems through RAG or other patterns.

requirements.name: Access Analysis for AI Resources
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure IAM Access Analyzer is enabled to validate access policies and identify unintended access to resources used by AI workloads.

requirements.name: Secrets Management for AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Secrets Manager is used for AI application credentials with automatic rotation enabled, restrictive resource policies, and no public access.

requirements.name: S3 Data Protection for AI
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure S3 buckets used for AI training data, model artifacts, RAG knowledge bases, and inference logs have public access blocked, encryption enabled, secure transport enforced, and access logging configured.

requirements.name: No Hardcoded Secrets in AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure no secrets or credentials are hardcoded in Lambda functions, ECS task definitions, or EC2 instances used as part of AI application architectures.

requirements.name: AI Services Data Opt-Out
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure the AWS Organization has opted out of all AI services data usage and child accounts cannot override this policy, preventing AWS from using customer data for AI service improvement.

requirements.name: Bedrock Guardrails Configuration
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Amazon Bedrock has at least one guardrail configured to provide content filtering, prompt injection defense, PII filtering, and topic restrictions for foundation model interactions.

requirements.name: Prompt Injection Defense
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock guardrails have prompt attack filter strength set to HIGH to detect and block prompt injection attempts, the #1 risk in OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

requirements.name: PII and Sensitive Data Filtering
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock guardrails block or mask sensitive information (PII) in both model inputs and outputs to prevent data leakage through AI responses.

requirements.name: Agent Guardrail Protection
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure all Bedrock agents have guardrails enabled to protect agent sessions from prompt injection, data exfiltration, and unauthorized actions during agentic workflows.

requirements.name: Model Invocation Logging
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock model invocation logging is enabled to maintain an immutable audit trail of all model interactions, enabling incident investigation and behavioral analysis.

requirements.name: Bedrock API Audit Trail
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure CloudTrail is configured to log all Bedrock API calls for security auditing, enabling detection of unauthorized model access, configuration changes, and potential LLM jacking.

requirements.name: Prompt Encryption and Management
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock prompts are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS keys and Prompt Management is used for centralized prompt governance.

requirements.name: Automated Reasoning for Output Validation
requirements.reason: An automated reasoning policy attached to a guardrail is a configuration signal. Application use of that guardrail and actual response verification accuracy require invocation traces and evaluation results.

new_checks.data_source: new read-only bedrock:ListAutomatedReasoningPolicies and bedrock:GetGuardrail (including versioned automatedReasoningPolicyConfig); application guardrail identifiers require workload inventory
new_checks.predicate: For each in-scope Bedrock application with a known guardrail identifier, fail if the referenced guardrail version has no configured automated reasoning policy ARN or the policy cannot be resolved as active; UNKNOWN when the application-to-guardrail binding is unavailable.
new_checks.title: Automated Reasoning for Output Validation
new_checks.description: Detects a Bedrock automated reasoning policy whose Bedrock automated-reasoning policy is not attached to the scoped guardrail; a guardrail without reasoning policy cannot validate model output against the approved rules.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Attach an active Automated Reasoning policy ARN to the versioned Bedrock guardrail used by each scoped application.

requirements.name: Contextual Grounding for RAG Validation
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock Contextual Grounding is configured to validate semantic consistency of model responses against sanctioned source documents, preventing hallucinated or fabricated outputs.

requirements.name: Knowledge Base Security for RAG
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock Knowledge Bases used for RAG patterns have proper security controls including encryption with customer-managed keys and VPC configuration for private data access.

requirements.name: WAF AI Activity Monitoring
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure WAF AI Activity Dashboard is configured to monitor and analyze AI-specific traffic patterns, providing visibility into potential attacks targeting AI endpoints.

requirements.name: Agent Identity and Authentication
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure every AI agent has its own identity with scoped credentials and independent authorization per request, following zero-trust principles. Agent identities must be separate from human user identities.

requirements.name: Agent Least-Privilege Authorization
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Bedrock AgentCore Cedar Policies enforce provable least-privilege authorization on every tool call and data access made by AI agents.

requirements.name: Agent Behavioral Monitoring
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure AI agents have behavioral monitoring and observability configured to detect scope violations, anomalous actions, and drift from expected behavior patterns.

requirements.name: Agent Registry and Catalog
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure a central agent registry exists to catalog all AI agents, their permissions, data access patterns, and operational boundaries for governance at scale.

requirements.name: Human Approval for Critical Agent Actions
requirements.reason: Ensure human-in-the-loop approval is required for high-consequence agent actions such as financial transactions, data deletion, or privilege changes — review agent action approval workflow and sampled high-consequence action approvals. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: ML Model Network Isolation
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure SageMaker models have network isolation enabled to prevent models from making unauthorized network calls during inference.

requirements.name: SageMaker Notebook Security
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure SageMaker notebook instances are secured with encryption, VPC settings, no direct internet access, and root access disabled.

requirements.name: ML Training Job Security
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure SageMaker training jobs have network isolation, VPC configuration, inter-container traffic encryption, and volume encryption enabled to protect training data and model weights.

requirements.name: Model Governance and Registry
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure SageMaker Model Registry is in use with approved model packages and SSO authentication is configured for SageMaker domains.

requirements.name: Model Monitoring and Bias Detection
requirements.reason: An active SageMaker monitoring schedule and recent Clarify job are technical signals. The check cannot establish continuous model-quality coverage or that bias thresholds are appropriate; review monitoring output and model governance records.

new_checks.data_source: sagemaker:ListMonitoringSchedules and DescribeMonitoringSchedule MonitoringScheduleConfig.MonitoringJobDefinition.MonitoringInputs[].EndpointInput.EndpointName, MonitoringScheduleConfig.MonitoringJobDefinition.BaselineConfig, MonitoringScheduleStatus; sagemaker:ListProcessingJobs and DescribeProcessingJob AppSpecification.ImageUri, ProcessingJobStatus, ProcessingInputs[].S3Input.S3Uri
new_checks.predicate: For each in-scope endpoint, FAIL if no ENABLED monitoring schedule names that endpoint or if no COMPLETED processing job with a Clarify image URI and a configured endpoint-linked input exists within the approved monitoring interval; UNKNOWN when endpoint-to-model linkage or the interval is unavailable.
new_checks.title: Model Monitoring and Bias Detection
new_checks.description: Detects a SageMaker processing job whose endpoint has no recent completed Clarify processing job and enabled schedule; missing Clarify runs leave model bias changes unobserved.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Enable an endpoint-linked SageMaker monitoring schedule and run a Clarify processing job within the approved interval.

requirements.name: Comprehensive Audit Logging
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions with multi-region logging, management event recording, log file validation, and CloudWatch integration for comprehensive AI workload audit trails.

requirements.name: GuardDuty Threat Detection
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure GuardDuty is enabled across all regions with delegated admin, S3 protection, EKS monitoring, Lambda protection, and malware protection to detect AI-specific threat patterns.

requirements.name: AI-Specific Threat Detection
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure CloudTrail-based threat detection is monitoring for LLM jacking, privilege escalation, and enumeration activity that could indicate attacks against AI infrastructure.

requirements.name: Security Hub Centralized Findings
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Security Hub is enabled with standards and integrations configured to aggregate and prioritize security findings across all AI workload services.

requirements.name: Security Event Alerting
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure CloudWatch metric filters and alarms are configured for critical security events including IAM policy changes, unauthorized API calls, console sign-in without MFA, KMS key deletion, and network changes.

requirements.name: AI Incident Investigation
requirements.reason: Detective graph presence is observable, but graph presence does not establish prompt-to-data-to-action decision-chain reconstruction; inspect application traces and investigation exercises.

new_checks.data_source: detective:ListGraphs GraphList[].Arn and GraphList[].CreatedTime in each in-scope account and region
new_checks.predicate: FAIL if an in-scope AI workload account/region has zero returned Detective GraphList entries with a nonempty Arn; UNKNOWN if the account/region inventory or ListGraphs result is unavailable.
new_checks.title: AI Incident Investigation
new_checks.description: Detects a Detective graph whose scoped account is absent from the enabled Detective graph; this can leave the workload exposed to preventable compromise or service loss.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Enable an Amazon Detective behavior graph and invite or associate each scoped account in its Region.

requirements.name: GuardDuty AI Threat Patterns
requirements.reason: The GuardDuty AI protection evaluator tests one protection setting. It does not establish detection of anomalous Bedrock API use, unusual model-access locations, or AI-channel exfiltration patterns.

requirements.name: Configuration Compliance Monitoring
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure AWS Config recorder is enabled in all regions to continuously monitor and record AI resource configurations, detect drift, and enforce compliance rules.

requirements.name: Organization Governance
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure the AWS account is part of an AWS Organization with proper governance controls including SCPs to restrict operations to approved regions and delegated administrators are trusted.

requirements.name: Security Contact Information
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure security contact information is registered and current for AI workload incident response communication.

requirements.name: Control Tower Automated Governance
requirements.reason: An ACTIVE Control Tower landing zone is a governance signal. It does not prove all AI workload accounts are enrolled or that their baselines are enforced; compare account inventory, OU enrollment and guardrail status.

new_checks.data_source: new read-only API call controltower:ListLandingZones + GetLandingZone with status
new_checks.predicate: Fail if no landing zone is ACTIVE for an organization hosting in-scope AI accounts; unknown if account-to-organization linkage is unavailable.
new_checks.title: Control Tower Automated Governance
new_checks.description: Detects a Control Tower landing zone whose Control Tower landing-zone status is not ACTIVE; this can leave the workload exposed to preventable compromise or service loss.
new_checks.remediation_hint: Create or update the Control Tower landing zone until GetLandingZone reports status ACTIVE for the scoped organization.

requirements.name: AI Workload Inventory and Audit
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Maintain an inventory of all AI workloads including approved and shadow AI usage. Document model selections, their governance requirements, and security evaluations.

requirements.name: AI Threat Modeling
requirements.reason: Ensure AI-specific threat models are developed before production deployment, covering prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration, model poisoning, and adversarial attacks — review approved AI threat model covering the named attack scenarios before production release. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: AI Incident Response Planning
requirements.reason: Ensure incident response plans include AI-specific scenarios covering prompt injection, model manipulation, data exfiltration through AI, LLM jacking, and agent scope violations — review approved AI incident-response plan and exercise records for the named scenarios. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: EKS Security for AI Runtimes
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure EKS clusters used for AI agent runtimes are properly secured with private endpoints, network policies, supported versions, control plane logging, and secrets encryption. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.eks.cluster_security_group_present: Only EKS cluster SG ID presence is observed. Pod NetworkPolicy enforcement and actual SG rules require separate checks; a missing modern ID is UNKNOWN. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: ECS Security for AI Workloads
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure ECS tasks used for AI workloads have no public IPs, no privileged containers, read-only root filesystems, logging enabled, and no secrets in environment variables.

requirements.name: Lambda Security for AI Functions
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Ensure Lambda functions used in AI architectures are deployed in VPCs, not publicly accessible, use supported runtimes, have no secrets in code or variables, and use CMK-encrypted environment variables.

requirements.name: Model Security Evaluation
requirements.reason: Perform security evaluation of foundation models before deployment, including assessment of input sanitization, access controls, bias audits, privacy disclosure, data poisoning resilience, adversarial resilience, and prompt injection defenses — review predeployment model security evaluation report with findings and disposition. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: Model Selection Governance
requirements.reason: Ensure model selection is appropriate for the use case with CISO involvement in evaluation. Customer-facing agents require different model security profiles than internal summarization tools — review model selection record, use-case assessment and CISO sign-off. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: When a port is exposed for non-SSH network traffic, all traffic MUST include a TLS handshake AND be encrypted using TLS 1.3 or higher.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: When a port is exposed for SSH network traffic, all traffic MUST include a SSH handshake AND be encrypted using SSHv2 or higher.

Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: When the service receives unencrypted traffic, then it MUST either block the request or automatically redirect it to the secure equivalent.

When a port is exposed, the service MUST ensure that the protocol and service officially assigned to that port number by the IANA Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry, and no other, is run on that port — review port-to-service inventory, approved service assignment and active protocol verification results. requirements.name: Article 25 Data protection by design and by default
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: To obtain the latest version of the official guide, please visit https://gdpr-info.eu/art-25-gdpr/. Taking into account the state of the art, the cost of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity for rights and freedoms of natural persons posed by the processing, the controller shall, both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner and to integrate the necessary safeguards into the processing in order to meet the requirements of this Regulation and protect the rights of data subjects. The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed. That obligation applies to the amount of personal data collected, the extent of their processing, the period of their storage and their accessibility. In particular, such measures shall ensure that by default personal data are not made accessible without the individual's intervention to an indefinite number of natural persons. An approved certification mechanism pursuant to Article 42 may be used as an element to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article.

requirements.name: Article 30 Records of processing activities
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: To obtain the latest version of the official guide, please visit https://www.privacy-regulation.eu/en/article-30-records-of-processing-activities-GDPR.htm. Each controller and, where applicable, the controller's representative, shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility. That record shall contain all of the following information like the name and contact details of the controller and where applicable, the joint controller, the controller's representative and the data protection officer, the purposes of the processing etc. Each processor and where applicable, the processor's representative shall maintain a record of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of a controller, containing the name and contact details of the processor or processors and of each controller on behalf of which the processor is acting, and, where applicable of the controller's or the processor's representative, and the data protection officer, where applicable, transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation, including the identification of that third country or international organisation and, in the case of transfers referred to in the second subparagraph of Article 49(1), the documentation of suitable safeguards. The records referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be in writing, including in electronic form. The controller or the processor and, where applicable, the controller's or the processor's representative, shall make the record available to the supervisory authority on request. The obligations referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to an enterprise or an organisation employing fewer than 250 persons unless the processing it carries out is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, the processing is not occasional, or the processing includes special categories of data as referred to in Article 9(1) or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10.

requirements.name: Article 32 Security of processing
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: To obtain the latest version of the official guide, please visit https://gdpr-info.eu/art-32-gdpr/. Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including inter alia as appropriate. In assessing the appropriate level of security account shall be taken in particular of the risks that are presented by processing, in particular from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed. Adherence to an approved code of conduct as referred to in Article 40 or an approved certification mechanism as referred to in Article 42 may be used as an element by which to demonstrate compliance with the requirements set out in paragraph 1 of this Article. The controller and processor shall take steps to ensure that any natural person acting under the authority of the controller or the processor who has access to personal data does not process them except on instructions from the controller, unless he or she is required to do so by Union or Member State law.

requirements.name: Secure Development Life Cycle
requirements.reason: Rules for the secure development of software and systems should be established and applied — review development or project procedure and sampled project records showing the named control was performed. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: Application Security Requirements
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Information security requirements should be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.

requirements.name: Secure Systems Architecture and Engineering Principles
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Principles for engineering secure systems should be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activities.

requirements.name: Security Testing in Development and Acceptance
requirements.reason: Security testing processes should be defined and implemented in the development life cycle — review development or project procedure and sampled project records showing the named control was performed. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: Outsourced Development
requirements.reason: The organisation should direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development — review development or project procedure and sampled project records showing the named control was performed. AWS read-only checks cannot attest the required operating behavior.

requirements.name: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Development, testing and production environments should be separated and secured.

requirements.name: Change Management
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Changes to information processing facilities and information systems should be subject to change management procedures.

requirements.name: Test Information
requirements.reason: Review test-data selection records, masking or protection procedures and sampled disposal evidence.

requirements.name: Protection of Information Systems During Audit Testing
requirements.reason: Review the preapproved operational audit-test plan, management agreement and completed test record.

requirements.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network. The weakness in the system can be a software bug, a temporary glitch, or a misconfiguration. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job: Configured DRS source replication state only. Required protection scope, recovery drills, launch settings and workload RTO require owner evidence. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: Trusted Relationship
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may breach or otherwise leverage organizations who have access to intended victims. Access through trusted third party relationship abuses an existing connection that may not be protected or receives less scrutiny than standard mechanisms of gaining access to a network.

requirements.name: Valid Accounts
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials may be used to bypass access controls placed on various resources on systems within the network and may even be used for persistent access to remote systems and externally available services, such as VPNs, Outlook Web Access, network devices, and remote desktop.[1] Compromised credentials may also grant an adversary increased privilege to specific systems or access to restricted areas of the network. Adversaries may choose not to use malware or tools in conjunction with the legitimate access those credentials provide to make it harder to detect their presence.

requirements.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces and languages provide ways of interacting with computer systems and are a common feature across many different platforms. Most systems come with some built-in command-line interface and scripting capabilities, for example, macOS and Linux distributions include some flavor of Unix Shell while Windows installations include the Windows Command Shell and PowerShell.

requirements.name: Serverless Execution
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may abuse serverless computing, integration, and automation services to execute arbitrary code in cloud environments. Many cloud providers offer a variety of serverless resources, including compute engines, application integration services, and web servers.

requirements.name: User Execution
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution. Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to execute malicious code by, for example, opening a malicious document file or link. These user actions will typically be observed as follow-on behavior from forms of Phishing.

requirements.name: Account Manipulation
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access to victim systems. Account manipulation may consist of any action that preserves adversary access to a compromised account, such as modifying credentials or permission groups. These actions could also include account activity designed to subvert security policies, such as performing iterative password updates to bypass password duration policies and preserve the life of compromised credentials.

requirements.name: Create Account
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems. With a sufficient level of access, creating such accounts may be used to establish secondary credentialed access that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

requirements.name: Implant Internal Image
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may implant cloud or container images with malicious code to establish persistence after gaining access to an environment. Amazon Web Services (AWS) Amazon Machine Images (AMIs), Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Images, and Azure Images as well as popular container runtimes such as Docker can be implanted or backdoored. Unlike Upload Malware, this technique focuses on adversaries implanting an image in a registry within a victim’s environment. Depending on how the infrastructure is provisioned, this could provide persistent access if the infrastructure provisioning tool is instructed to always use the latest image.

requirements.name: Modify Authentication Process
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may modify authentication mechanisms and processes to access user credentials or enable otherwise unwarranted access to accounts. The authentication process is handled by mechanisms, such as the Local Security Authentication Server (LSASS) process and the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) on Windows, pluggable authentication modules (PAM) on Unix-based systems, and authorization plugins on MacOS systems, responsible for gathering, storing, and validating credentials. By modifying an authentication process, an adversary may be able to authenticate to a service or system without using Valid Accounts.

requirements.name: Impair Defenses
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may maliciously modify components of a victim environment in order to hinder or disable defensive mechanisms. This not only involves impairing preventative defenses, such as firewalls and anti-virus, but also detection capabilities that defenders can use to audit activity and identify malicious behavior. This may also span both native defenses as well as supplemental capabilities installed by users and administrators.

requirements.name: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: An adversary may attempt to modify a cloud account's compute service infrastructure to evade defenses. A modification to the compute service infrastructure can include the creation, deletion, or modification of one or more components such as compute instances, virtual machines, and snapshots.

requirements.name: Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may create cloud instances in unused geographic service regions in order to evade detection. Access is usually obtained through compromising accounts used to manage cloud infrastructure.

requirements.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may use alternate authentication material, such as password hashes, Kerberos tickets, and application access tokens, in order to move laterally within an environment and bypass normal system access controls.

requirements.name: Brute Force
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. Without knowledge of the password for an account or set of accounts, an adversary may systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism. Brute forcing passwords can take place via interaction with a service that will check the validity of those credentials or offline against previously acquired credential data, such as password hashes.

requirements.name: Forge Web Credentials
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may forge credential materials that can be used to gain access to web applications or Internet services. Web applications and services (hosted in cloud SaaS environments or on-premise servers) often use session cookies, tokens, or other materials to authenticate and authorize user access.

requirements.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
requirements.reason: CloudTrail CreateVirtualMFADevice, EnableMFADevice and ResyncMFADevice do not record user-facing MFA push generation or fatigue; inspect identity-provider MFA challenge logs and correlated user reports.

requirements.name: Network Sniffing
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may sniff network traffic to capture information about an environment, including authentication material passed over the network. Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection. An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data.

requirements.name: Unsecured Credentials
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may search compromised systems to find and obtain insecurely stored credentials. These credentials can be stored and/or misplaced in many locations on a system, including plaintext files (e.g. Bash History), operating system or application-specific repositories (e.g. Credentials in Registry), or other specialized files/artifacts (e.g. Private Keys).

requirements.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing command and control channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main command and control server.

requirements.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may exfiltrate data by transferring the data, including backups of cloud environments, to another cloud account they control on the same service to avoid typical file transfers/downloads and network-based exfiltration detection.

requirements.name: Automated Collection
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data. Methods for performing this technique could include use of a Command and Scripting Interpreter to search for and copy information fitting set criteria such as file type, location, or name at specific time intervals. In cloud-based environments, adversaries may also use cloud APIs, command line interfaces, or extract, transform, and load (ETL) services to automatically collect data. This functionality could also be built into remote access tools.

requirements.name: Data from Cloud Storage
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may collect sensitive data from these cloud storage solutions. Providers typically offer security guides to help end users configure systems, though misconfigurations are a common problem.[5][6][7] There have been numerous incidents where cloud storage has been improperly secured, typically by unintentionally allowing public access to unauthenticated users, overly-broad access by all users, or even access for any anonymous person outside the control of the Identity Access Management system without even needing basic user permissions.

requirements.name: Data Destruction
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may destroy data and files on specific systems or in large numbers on a network to interrupt availability to systems, services, and network resources. Data destruction is likely to render stored data irrecoverable by forensic techniques through overwriting files or data on local and remote drives.[1][2][3][4][5][6] Common operating system file deletion commands such as del and rm often only remove pointers to files without wiping the contents of the files themselves, making the files recoverable by proper forensic methodology. This behavior is distinct from Disk Content Wipe and Disk Structure Wipe because individual files are destroyed rather than sections of a storage disk or the disk's logical structure. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job: Configured DRS source replication state only. Required protection scope, recovery drills, launch settings and workload RTO require owner evidence. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or on large numbers of systems in a network to interrupt availability to system and network resources. They can attempt to render stored data inaccessible by encrypting files or data on local and remote drives and withholding access to a decryption key. This may be done in order to extract monetary compensation from a victim in exchange for decryption or a decryption key (ransomware) or to render data permanently inaccessible in cases where the key is not saved or transmitted. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job: Configured DRS source replication state only. Required protection scope, recovery drills, launch settings and workload RTO require owner evidence. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: Defacement
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may modify visual content available internally or externally to an enterprise network, thus affecting the integrity of the original content. Reasons for Defacement include delivering messaging, intimidation, or claiming (possibly false) credit for an intrusion. Disturbing or offensive images may be used as a part of Defacement in order to cause user discomfort, or to pressure compliance with accompanying messages. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job: Configured DRS source replication state only. Required protection scope, recovery drills, launch settings and workload RTO require owner evidence. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may perform Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users. Endpoint DoS can be performed by exhausting the system resources those services are hosted on or exploiting the system to cause a persistent crash condition. Example services include websites, email services, DNS, and web-based applications. Adversaries have been observed conducting DoS attacks for political purposes[1] and to support other malicious activities, including distraction[2], hacktivism, and extortion.

requirements.name: Inhibit System Recovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in data and turn off services designed to aid in the recovery of a corrupted system to prevent recovery.[1][2] This may deny access to available backups and recovery options. Corrected native semantic scope: aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job: Configured DRS source replication state only. Required protection scope, recovery drills, launch settings and workload RTO require owner evidence. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

requirements.name: Resource Hijacking
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may leverage the resources of co-opted systems in order to solve resource intensive problems, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability.

requirements.name: Network Denial of Service
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users. Network DoS can be performed by exhausting the network bandwidth services rely on. Example resources include specific websites, email services, DNS, and web-based applications. Adversaries have been observed conducting network DoS attacks for political purposes[1] and to support other malicious activities, including distraction[2], hacktivism, and extortion.

requirements.name: Account Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment. This information can help adversaries determine which accounts exist, which can aid in follow-on behavior such as brute-forcing, spear-phishing attacks, or account takeovers (e.g., Valid Accounts).

requirements.name: Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: An adversary may attempt to discover infrastructure and resources that are available within an infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environment. This includes compute service resources such as instances, virtual machines, and snapshots as well as resources of other services including the storage and database services.

requirements.name: Cloud Service Dashboard
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: An adversary may use a cloud service dashboard GUI with stolen credentials to gain useful information from an operational cloud environment, such as specific services, resources, and features. For example, the GCP Command Center can be used to view all assets, findings of potential security risks, and to run additional queries, such as finding public IP addresses and open ports.

requirements.name: Cloud Service Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: An adversary may attempt to enumerate the cloud services running on a system after gaining access. These methods can differ from platform-as-a-service (PaaS), to infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), or software-as-a-service (SaaS). Many services exist throughout the various cloud providers and can include Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD), Lambda Functions, Azure AD, etc. They may also include security services, such as AWS GuardDuty and Microsoft Defender for Cloud, and logging services, such as AWS CloudTrail and Google Cloud Audit Logs.

requirements.name: Cloud Storage Object Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may enumerate objects in cloud storage infrastructure. Adversaries may use this information during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including requesting all or specific objects from cloud storage. Similar to File and Directory Discovery on a local host, after identifying available storage services (i.e. Cloud Infrastructure Discovery) adversaries may access the contents/objects stored in cloud infrastructure.

requirements.name: Network Service Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation. Common methods to acquire this information include port and/or vulnerability scans using tools that are brought onto a system.

requirements.name: Password Policy Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may attempt to access detailed information about the password policy used within an enterprise network or cloud environment. Password policies are a way to enforce complex passwords that are difficult to guess or crack through Brute Force. This information may help the adversary to create a list of common passwords and launch dictionary and/or brute force attacks which adheres to the policy (e.g. if the minimum password length should be 8, then not trying passwords such as 'pass123'; not checking for more than 3-4 passwords per account if the lockout is set to 6 as to not lock out accounts).

requirements.name: System Network Connections Discovery
requirements.reason: EC2 DescribeNetworkInterfaces and DescribeSecurityGroups are cloud configuration inventory calls, not evidence that a host queried live network connections; inspect host process and network telemetry.

requirements.name: System Location Discovery
requirements.reason: DescribeRegions and DescribeAvailabilityZones return AWS region inventory, not a victim host’s physical or logical location discovery; inspect host command and application telemetry.

requirements.name: System Information Discovery
requirements.reason: EC2 DescribeInstances and DescribeAccountAttributes do not reveal the guest OS version, patches or hardware enumeration attempted by the technique; inspect host command and endpoint telemetry.
